item.title: Characterization and Monte Carlo Simulation of Wavelength-Shifting Absorption Length in Plastic Optical Fibers
item.description: arXiv:2611.28021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report an experimental characterization of the wavelength-shifting (WLS) absorption length of the EJ-160I fiber core material from Eljen Technology. Fiber-core samples of different thicknesses were employed, and the transmitted intensity of incident LED light was measured to extract the WLS absorption length at 405.7 nm. The resulting value, (0.823 +/- 0.038) mm, was used to normalize the WLS absorption length spectrum derived from the absorption spectrum of the core material. An independent measurement at 392.5 nm yielded a WLS absorption length of (1.404 +/- 0.074) mm, differing from the value predicted by the reconstructed WLS absorption length spectrum by 3.16%, corresponding to 0.43 sigma. The resulting spectrum was implemented as an optical input in a Geant4-based optical Monte Carlo simulation of the EJ-160I fiber to examine the role of the WLS absorption length in light output, light attenuation, and the emission spectrum.
item.dc:creator: W. Bae, L. Baker, K. Chen, J. Cho, K. Lang, C. Lee, E. Liang, C. Mathurin, C. Murthy, D. Myers, S. Nguyen, M. Proga, M. Zalikha, J. Zey

item.title: Towards Automatic Ion Identification in Storage Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.28070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonant Schottky detectors provide non-destructive, single-ion-sensitive measurements of revolution frequencies and intensities of ion species stored in a heavy-ion storage ring. These high-\(Q\) cavities allow analysis of high-order harmonics of the revolution frequencies to magnify absolute frequency separations. Adjacent harmonic ranges can, however, overlap within the detector band, making frequency alone insufficient for determining the ion's mass-to-charge ratio $(m/q)$. We present a proof-of-concept for an automated harmonic de-overlapping method using spectral shapes in combined Schottky and Isochronous Mass Spectrometry. The empirical ansatz is that, for a fixed ion-optical setting, each peak, corresponding to a specific ion species with given $m/q$ ratio, has a characteristic profile that evolves smoothly with changing $m/q$. Occurrences of the same local structure at different harmonics should therefore retain almost identical shapes after frequency rescaling. Applied to a 245\,MHz spectrum accumulated from 11\,452 injections at the Experimental Storage Ring at GSI, the method organizes 16 of 32 detected structures into five candidate families and reconstructs their fundamental-frequency representation. Reducing the complex mixed-harmonic spectrum to this smaller candidate set solves the challenging task of finding initial anchors for the ion identification.
item.dc:creator: Anna Jule He{\ss}, David Freire-Fern\'andez, Moritz Porstend\"orfer, Wolfram Korten, Yury A. Litvinov

item.title: HEP-like 1550 nm wide-field pixelated optical receiver for inter-satellite laser links: a simulation-based proof of concept for Earth, lunar and Earth-Moon scenarios
item.description: arXiv:2611.28071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I propose and evaluate by simulation a wide-field dome optical receiver (a field of view larger than a hemisphere) at 1550 nm for the acquisition of inter-satellite laser links. The detector is an InGaAs pixel hybrid of about 1 Mpixel with event-driven, time-stamped readout, inspired by the pixel detectors of high-energy physics. A pulsed beacon is detected by the coincidence of m hits in a sliding block of pixels, and the angle of arrival (AoA) is estimated by clustering and centroiding and handed to a narrow-field data channel. In a 550 km Earth constellation, with a 5 mrad beacon and a 10 mm aperture, detection takes 12 $\mu$s to 2 ms (up to 116 ms with the 6-9 mm that the optics allow), with a whole-frame false-alarm rate below 0.01/s, and the AoA error is 0.13-0.23 mrad. Cooling to about 233 K gives a service life above 5 years for fluences up to about $2\times10^{9}$ p/cm$^2$ per year. The receiver is also studied around the Moon and on the Earth-Moon link, where it works only between high orbits. Compared phase by phase with published scan-based acquisition, the search phase (3-18 ms with 10 mm) is shorter by a factor of about $10^{2}$ to $10^{5}$; end to end, with assumed pointing and loop-closure times, it takes 0.16-1.5 s, comparable to a terminal with calibrated open-loop pointing but without requiring that pointing at the receiver; the partner's beacon must still be pointed at it to about 1.25 mrad (5 mrad beacon). All values are simulation results, obtained with idealised optics and a 1 Mpixel detector that does not exist today; none is a measurement.
item.dc:creator: Maurizio De Santis

item.title: Design and performance of a top-loading vibrating-sample magnetometer for a helium-flow variable-temperature insert
item.description: arXiv:2611.28072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a custom-built top-loading probe that adds vibrating-sample magnetometry to an existing helium-flow variable-temperature insert without replacing its cryogenic or magnetic-field infrastructure. The modular instrument combines a detachable sealed drive head, a voice-coil resonator operating near 44 Hz, continuous monitoring of the peak vibration amplitude, motorized axial centering, and a compact first-order pickup-coil gradiometer. A numerical flux-linkage calculation reproduces the position and shape of the measured axial response for several vibration amplitudes after multiplication by a common factor of 1.08. Measurements on Ni reference samples demonstrate operation down to 5 K and yield effective geometrical factors between 24.0 V s A$^{-1}$ m$^{-3}$ and 31.4 V s A$^{-1}$ m$^{-3}$. At fixed field, the observed voltage scatter corresponds to moment-equivalent one-standard-deviation repeatabilities of 16.5 nA m$^{2}$ to 27.8 nA m$^{2}$. For a 31.7 nm Ni film measured at 250 K, magnetization curves obtained at three vibration amplitudes approximately collapse after amplitude correction and yield a saturation magnetization of approximately 409 kA m$^{-1}$ after subtraction of the linear high-field background. The results demonstrate a practical retrofit approach for adding bulk and thin-film magnetometry to VTIs with comparable bore and flange constraints.
item.dc:creator: Alfons G. Schuck, Sebastian K\"olsch, J\"org Franke, Michael Huth

item.title: A Multimode-Fiber Speckle Sensing Node with a Press-Robust Quantized Network for Liquid-Cooling Thermal Monitoring
item.description: arXiv:2611.28091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Liquid-cooled AI and HPC racks concentrate heat at cold plates and manifolds, below the granularity of facility sensors. We present a self-contained edge node that turns one multimode fiber into a distributed thermal-event sensor over nine pipe segments, with a 450 nm laser, a camera and a Zynq UltraScale+ device that captures, infers, displays and reports over MQTT. The speckle decorrelates within tens of seconds at constant temperature, and a press can change it as much as a 1 degree Celsius rise. The node averages each 20 s window and feeds two planes, the mean pattern and a 19-dimensional temporal-feature map, to a 61.6k-parameter int8 convolutional neural network (CNN) that treats presses as hard negatives and runs in the programmable logic at 565 microseconds per frame. On a 59-session, 70,148-window dataset, session-held-out validation gives a pooled AUC of 0.961 against 0.876 for decorrelation, no alarm during the hold or the 45 s rebound in 23 press trials against 6 and 16, and a mean per-fold step detection of 83.8% at 0.4 false alarms per hour.
item.dc:creator: Xuezhi Lou, Weipeng Zhang, Zhibai Zhang, Liyuan Ren

item.title: In-pixel lock-in readout for wide-field nitrogen-vacancy radio-frequency spectrum analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.28121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing use of radio-frequency (RF) technologies requires compact, room-temperature sensors that can analyze a wide RF band in real time. Here we present a quantum RF spectrum analyzer based on the gradient-encoded electron spin resonance of a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensemble in diamond and read out with a $512\times542$-pixel lock-in camera that demodulates the signal in each pixel. On/off keying the signal under test at the camera's reference frequency lets every pixel extract the spin-resonant photoluminescence modulation. Before digitization, each pixel suppresses the static background and low-frequency noise that limit conventional camera readout. Translating a single permanent magnet tunes the encoded band continuously from 10~MHz to 32~GHz. The magnet position establishes a trade-off between instantaneous bandwidth (up to 4~GHz) and frequency resolution (7--22~MHz), with a 5~ms readout time. The wide-field readout integrates all spectral channels in parallel in a room-temperature sensor head and requires no phase synchronization to the RF carrier. The SNR remains above 70 at an applied power as low as $-32.5$~dBm. The magnetic-field configuration can be adapted to different RF bands without changing the pixel-parallel readout.
item.dc:creator: Shihao Ru, Jiakai Chen, Xiaodan Lyu, Mingyu Hao, Zitong Xu, Edwin Hang Tong Teo, Fedor Jelezko, Jesus Z\'u\~niga-Pere, Weibo Gao

item.title: lawless: Normalization, Scaling, and Merging of Laue Data in the AIMLESS Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.28131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: lawless, a new program for wavelength normalization, scaling, and merging of Laue data from both X-rays and neutrons, is presented. Based on the AIMLESS program, lawless provides two methods of wavelength normalization via Chebyshev polynomials and Gaussian process regression, the latter of which is a more general method for various sources. Coupled with AIMLESS gentler outlier rejection methodology and superior error modelling, lawless provides better quality neutron maps than previous methods by focusing on completeness over better-looking merging statistics. Even as R-factors increase and CC1/2 numbers decrease, dataset completeness is the biggest limiting factor in neutron map quality and should be a primary focus in data reduction.
item.dc:creator: Aaron D. Finke

item.title: Label-free self-calibration of a segmented HPGe $\gamma$-ray tracking array from the Compton scattering constraint
item.description: arXiv:2611.28142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pulse-shape analysis in segmented HPGe $\gamma$-ray tracking arrays such as AGATA relies on reference signals for known interaction positions, which are costly to measure and only approximate when calculated. In a simulation of 51 AGATA crystals, we show that the interaction positions can be learned from the pulses without position labels. For a \Co\ photon that is Compton scattered in one segment and absorbed in another, the scattering angle follows both from the deposited energies and from the positions of the source and of the two interactions. A neural network shared by all crystals predicts one position per fired segment and is trained only to make these two angles agree; the unmeasured order of the two interactions and the selection of the pairs are revised during training. The pulses, synthesised from AGATAGeFEM bases for $2.79\times10^{6}$ pairs of fired segments whose energies add up to a \Co\ line, selected from $4\times10^{7}$ simulated decays, include noise, cross-talk, trigger-time jitter and differences between crystals. For the hits of held-out pairs, the mean three-dimensional position error falls from 10.4~mm with the segment centres to 1.65~mm, with a FWHM of 1.0--1.3~mm in each coordinate, compared with 1.07~mm for the same network trained on the simulated positions. The constraint determines the positions along the crystal axes only weakly, and at small scattering angles it pulls low-energy first interactions towards the source, which is why deposits below 200~keV are excluded. Even with the simulated positions, the two angles differ, mainly because a segment with several interactions is described by a single position and energy rather than because of Doppler broadening.
item.dc:creator: Mojahed Abushawish, J\'er\'emie Dudouet, Olivier St\'ezowski, Jos\'e Manuel Ud\'ias

item.title: Machine-learning-assisted photon pairing for neutral-pion reconstruction at future Higgs factories
item.description: arXiv:2611.28180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neutral-pion ($\pi^0$) reconstruction is important for precision measurements at high-energy colliders, particularly in flavor, $\tau$, and Higgs physics. We study $\pi^0$ candidate selection in four benchmark physics processes at electron--positron colliders, comparing an optimized diphoton mass-window (MW) baseline with four machine-learning methods: a boosted decision tree (BDT), a multilayer perceptron (MLP), ParticleNet (PN), and Particle Transformer (ParT). Performance is evaluated using the product of selection efficiency and purity. At the reference ECAL energy resolution, all four machine-learning methods outperform MW. PN and ParT achieve relative improvements of 53%--95% and 60%--128%, respectively, primarily through better rejection of incorrectly matched photon pairs. Their performance advantage is maintained across the investigated ECAL energy resolutions. Training-sample-size scans reveal two periods of rapid performance improvement separated by slower growth in most PN and ParT learning curves. The improved candidate selection provides a starting point for further studies of $\rho$ and hadronic $\tau$ reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Yi Wang, Chao Yang, Tianyi Yang, Enrui Tian, Yuexin Wang, Song Pan, Jun Guo, Manqi Ruan

item.title: CHARMS250V1: A Cryogenic Front-End ASIC for Low-Noise Readout of Charge or Light Signals in Noble Liquid Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2611.28269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. It comprises pre-amplification and pulse shaping stages that provide programmable charge gain between 4.3 mV/fC and 25 mV/fC, peaking time programmable between 250 ns and 2 us, and programmable baseline of either 200 mV or 900 mV for processing of unipolar and bipolar signals, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Prashansa Mukim, Shanshan Gao, Hucheng Chen, Grzegorz W. Deptuch, Jack Fried, Niccolo' Gallice, Dominik Gorni, Lingyun Ke, Giovanni Pinaroli, Sergio Rescia, Chao Zhang

item.title: Real-time event-level zero-shot learning at 150 ns: towards a foundation model for particle physics experiment triggering
item.description: arXiv:2611.28355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hardware-based Level-1 triggers of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments select collisions with algorithms designed for one signature each, acting on a coarse, low-latency view of every event. We present a learned event embedding for several trigger tasks and evaluate its transfer to processes absent from training. Using paired offline and Level-1 views of the same simulated collisions, we train an offline transformer with a supervised metric loss and distil it, event by event, into a quantised Level-1 transformer whose bit widths are learned under a fixed resource budget. Trained on 25 Standard Model processes, the embedding places 28 held-out processes next to their physical relatives. A nearest-neighbour selection against background collisions, which never enter encoder training, rejects 99% of them. It retains a median of 90% of seen and 96% of unseen Standard Model events and 88% of a set of 52 beyond-the-Standard-Model benchmark samples, the best-performing score across the three groups among the baselines evaluated on the same events. A second gate against the seen processes isolates high-mass dilepton signals into label-free clusters, and long-lived signals too when displaced-track information is available. With 7512 parameters and an FPGA latency of 147 ns, the encoder uses one event representation, learned once, to derive several selections, opening the door to a foundation model for the LHC's hardware-based triggers.
item.dc:creator: Leo Rozanov, Lauri Laatu, Benedikt Maier, Arianna Cox, Aadeesh Sharma, Zhiqiang Que, Alex Tapper

item.title: A high-speed and high-resolution 3D velocity map imaging system with a neuromorphic camera
item.description: arXiv:2611.28768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An improved camera-based 3D-velocity map imaging (VMI) system was demonstrated with a neuromorphic camera. We show a machine vision event-driven camera can achieve an unprecedented latency of 2 microseconds when detecting single ion/electron with a microchannel plate imaging detector, which boosts the speed of the momentum imaging system to more than 100 kHz, while the system with a conventional frame camera is limited to a few kHz. The high spatial resolution of the camera offers additional performance boost while maintaining excellent multi-hit capability and a high time resolution.
item.dc:creator: Sulaiman Abubakar, Blessed Oguh, Akaninyene Udoikono, Hackim Musah, Suk Kyoung Lee, Wen Li

item.title: Ion Backflow Suppression and Absorption Dynamics in Cascaded GEM Structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.28806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ion backflow (IBF) is a persistent challenge in Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) detectors: positive ions drifting back into the sensitive volume distort the drift field and degrade both spatial and energy resolution. We investigate the ion-absorption characteristics of single- to quintuple-GEM detectors using ANSYS and Garfield$^{++}$ for an Ar/CO$_2$ (70:30) gas mixture. A layer-resolved formalism is developed that distinguishes conditional foil-level absorption from a detector-level absorption metric that correctly weights ion production at every amplification stage. For the conventional biconical geometry, cascading foils improves the overall ion-absorption fraction only moderately, from 47.83\% for a single GEM to 59.06\% for a quintuple GEM. Replacing the biconical holes with a single-conical profile raises the absorption fraction to 75\%-87\% across the same range of multiplicities and reduces the IBF/Gain ratio by a factor of two to three an improvement that exceeds what is gained by adding four additional biconical foils. As a secondary test under more realistic conditions, the second transfer-gap length of a triple-GEM detector is varied from 1.2 to 3.5~mm. The gain shows a non-monotonic dependence with a maximum near 2.0-2.5~mm, while the IBF/Gain ratio decreases monotonically with increasing gap length; the single-conical geometry retains its factor-of-two advantage throughout. These findings establish that ion suppression in cascaded GEM structures is governed not only by the number of foils but primarily by the local ion-collection properties of each foil, and that single-conical holes represent a promising route to improved performance in high-rate detector applications.
item.dc:creator: Md Kaosor Ali Mondal, Shakir Eqbal, Sachin Rana, Poojan Angiras, A. Sarkar

item.title: Data handling, production, and simulation in the Muon g-2 Experiment at Fermilab
item.description: arXiv:2611.28851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper details the computing strategies of the Muon g-2 Experiment at Fermilab, which measured the muon's anomalous magnetic moment with a precision of 127 ppb by processing over 10 petabytes of detector and simulation data. This paper discusses the computational and operational challenges of data production, data handling, and data analysis of such large datasets. These challenges were overcome by using Fermilab-developed software infrastructure and production tools, making efficient use of resources, and improving the collaboration-developed reconstruction workflow. By overcoming these challenges, the experiment improved the data throughput capacity and reduced the analysis turnaround time by an order of magnitude over the course of its lifetime.

item.title: A Camera-Based Single-Volume, Monolithic Compton Camera
item.description: arXiv:2611.29116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Compton camera measures two events in a detector from individual gamma-rays to reconstruct the radiation source. Conventional scintillator-based Compton cameras consist of two separate scintillator volumes or a single segmented scintillator, resulting in drawbacks regarding detector bulkiness and efficiency. Their scintillator readout techniques struggle to resolve two nearby events in one monolithic scintillator. Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) cameras have recently been proposed for measuring scintillation events in various configurations. SPAD array sensors enable high-resolution photon-counting acquisition at high rates that is easily scalable to millions of pixels. Prior work has explored different optics and measurement arrangements as well as demonstrated measurement of single interaction locations. In this work, we extend these capabilities to demonstrate a practical radiation imaging device in the form of a Compton camera consisting of a SPAD camera and one compact, monolithic scintillator. Our Compton camera prototype successfully reconstructs a gamma-ray source over multiple locations that span a 4$\pi$ steradian field of view. Our approach is able to resolve two simultaneous events in one monolithic scintillator and enables Compton camera devices with compact, monolithic scintillator volumes for enhanced portability.
item.dc:creator: Alex Bocchieri, Devanshi Jain, Andreas Velten

item.title: Simulation and Rejection of Radon Progeny Backgrounds in nEXO
item.description: arXiv:2611.29172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radon-induced backgrounds from $^{214}$Bi decays remain a significant challenge for liquid xenon (LXe) detectors searching for neutrinoless double beta decay ($0\nu\beta\beta$). We present a simulation-based study of the $^{214}$Bi background in nEXO, incorporating a physically motivated model of the transport and implantation of radon progeny into the detector cathode. We show that the spatial distribution of scintillation light provides an additional method for background discrimination for events surviving standard energy, event topology, and fiducial volume selections. A simple discriminator based on the scintillation light detected below the cathode rejects 41% of the remaining $^{214}$Bi backgrounds while retaining 95% of $0\nu\beta\beta$ signal events, and a convolutional neural network classifier improves this rejection to 57% at the same signal efficiency. An updated optical model provides a more accurate estimate of the light collection efficiency below the cathode than used in previous work, increasing the expected $^{214}$Bi-$^{214}$Po (Bi-Po) coincidence-tagging efficiency for bottom-surface $^{214}$Bi decays from less than 1% to approximately 50%. Together, these results demonstrate improved rejection of cathode-implanted $^{214}$Bi backgrounds in nEXO through complementary prompt scintillation-based discrimination and delayed coincidence tagging.

item.title: Development of a Hybrid Scintillator Strip-Drift Tube Muon Detector for the FCC-ee
item.description: arXiv:2611.29331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee) is a proposed high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ collider for precision measurements at the electroweak, Higgs, and top-quark energy scales. A high-performance, cost-effective muon system is essential for muon identification, triggering, momentum measurement, and long-lived particle detection. We present the R&D of a hybrid muon detector concept combining fast extruded plastic scintillator strips with precision drift tubes. The scintillator strips were produced at Fermilab, while detector prototypes with SiPM readout and pressurized drift tubes were designed, constructed, and integrated at the University of Michigan. The hybrid detector was tested at the CERN test beam facility in 2025 and 2026. The scintillator strips achieved a position resolution of 1.6 mm and a time resolution of approximately 350 ps, while the drift tubes provided a single-hit spatial resolution better than 100 $\mu$m. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a high-performance hybrid muon spectrometer for the FCC-ee.
item.dc:creator: Jiajin Ge (on behalf of the University of Michigan FCC-ee R&D team)

item.title: A Theoretical Investigation of Magnetic Susceptibility Measurement of Diamagnetic Liquids Using a Michelson Interferometer
item.description: arXiv:2611.29671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the theoretical use of a Michelson interferometer to infer the magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic liquid from a magnetically induced surface deformation. A ring magnet changes the liquid thickness along the sample beam, producing a signed phase shift relative to a fixed optical reference. For a double traversal of the sample, the fringe displacement is $m = 2(n_{\ell} - n_a)\Delta z/\lambda$. We derive the susceptibility inversion both in a local gravity approximation and with surface tension included through the linearized Young-Laplace equation. The treatment distinguishes a finite reference field from a zero-field reference, specifies the displacement sign and susceptibility contrast, and identifies calibration and uncertainty requirements. Reproducible illustrative calculations use a uniformly magnetized annulus. The results establish a theoretical measurement relation and its assumptions; they do not constitute an experimental demonstration or a verified accuracy claim.
item.dc:creator: David Shulman

item.title: An eight-channel RFSoC waveform digitizer with AC- and DC-coupled front ends and transparent dual-DDR event memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.29881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Transparent Dual-DDR Event Memory (TDEM) for the triggered readout of an eight-channel radio-frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) digitizer. With either an AC- or a DC-coupled front end, each accepted trigger records 4096 samples per channel at 5 GSa/s. Two pulses 100 ns apart produced separate, overlapping records. On one DC-coupled input, interleaving calibration reduced an eight-sample periodic residual by a factor of 29 at +100 mV, but not at zero input. After a power cycle, the digitizer restored the coefficients for all eight DC-coupled inputs without a training tone. TDEM assigns complete events to 64- and 32-bit DDR4 memory interfaces in a 2:1 ratio. With this allocation alone, host page requests still determined which memory served each read. In two runs of approximately 6 s at 160 kHz, the peak receiver backlog fell from 20 140 events with the earlier readout to 1457 with event-level prefetch. Prefetch raised the sustained rate of the DC-coupled system from 150 to 170 kHz under repeated host readout pauses. With the same receiver design and a revised host buffer allocation, the AC-coupled system passed three 30 min tests at 175 kHz, each with 48 readout pauses and no rejected triggers. Without imposed pauses or background load, the host verified all 323 452 631 events in 30 min at 179.7 kHz. At 180 kHz, triggers were first rejected at the digitizer, consistent with a modelled transmitter capacity of 179.730 kHz for this event format.
item.dc:creator: Tao Xue

item.title: XTCP: an open-source FPGA TCP endpoint for readout over 10 and 25 Gigabit Ethernet
item.description: arXiv:2611.29921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: XTCP is an open-source implementation of the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) for high-rate detector readout. It targets sustained single-connection throughput near the TCP payload limit. In separate 10 Gigabit Ethernet transfers on the same Kintex UltraScale+ KU5P card and Linux host, XTCP and SiTCP-XG each delivered a median application-level throughput of 9.49 Gbit/s towards the host. Towards the FPGA, the medians were 9.49 Gbit/s for XTCP and 5.76 Gbit/s for the tested SiTCP-XG configuration. The XTCP prototype used more lookup tables and on-chip memory. In a 96 GiB echo test spanning repeated sequence-number wraps, recording when an acknowledgement first crossed the recovery boundary allowed four fast recoveries that the earlier signed comparison would have blocked. On one 25 Gigabit Ethernet bitstream, increasing the IP maximum transmission unit from 1500 to 9000 bytes raised median one-way throughput from 23.30 to 24.70 Gbit/s towards the host and from 22.09 to 24.08 Gbit/s towards the FPGA. At 9000 bytes these rates reached 99.7% and 97.1% of the TCP payload limit, respectively. In a separate echo test, the host verified all 8.77 TB returned by a jumbo-frame prototype over one connection in 3595 s, averaging 19.51 Gbit/s per direction.
item.dc:creator: Tao Xue

item.title: A Novel Multi-Target Approach for simultaneous enhancement of brightness, intensity, and bi-spectral performance of cold neutron sources
item.description: arXiv:2611.30086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Increasing the brightness of cold neutron beams is a central objective in modern cold neutron source development, since it largely governs the sample intensity for high-resolution neutron instruments. Raising accelerator beam power is constrained by the target heat-removal limit of 0.5-1 kW/cm2, and increasing the moderator length beyond about 20-30 cm becomes inefficient owing to the finite mean free path of cold neutrons. We propose reversing the conventional design logic: rather than tailoring the cryogenic moderator to a fixed target-premoderator source, we tailor the thermal-neutron source geometry to a high-performance moderator configuration. The concept is realized as a staircase moderator assembly of several shorter compressed moderators, each with its own target-premoderator unit, which distributes neutron production among multiple units and thus enables higher accelerator powers while preserving the brightness advantages of compressed moderators. This approach can provide additional brightness and intensity gains relative to a single low-dimensional or conventional voluminous moderator at the desired transverse beam size and may naturally generate bi-spectral neutron beams, thereby extending the dynamic range of neutron instruments.
item.dc:creator: A. Ioffe, P. Konik, D. Shapiro

item.title: High-rate accumulation of ${8.9\times10^9}$ positrons using a linac-driven buffer-gas trap combined with a SiC remoderator
item.description: arXiv:2611.30238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the accumulation of $(8.9 \pm 0.9)\times10^9$ positrons in less than 35 minutes in a Penning--Malmberg trap connected to the GBAR electron-linac-based positron source. To our knowledge, this exceeds the largest previously reported trapped-positron population by more than a factor of two and was achieved at an 18-fold higher average accumulation rate of $4.5\times10^6$~e$^+$/s. The accumulated positron clouds are intended for the creation of dense positronium targets to produce keV-antihydrogen beams by charge exchange with antiprotons delivered by the CERN AD/ELENA facility. The system combines a low-energy electron linac, a modified Surko-type buffer-gas trap enhanced by a silicon carbide remoderator, and a high-field Penning--Malmberg trap operated as a positron accumulator. Time-resolved annihilation measurements provide insight into the capture and cooling dynamics, while comparisons of CO$_2$ and SF$_6$ show that the trapping signal reaches saturation at lower gas pressures with SF$_6$. Measurements show that the SiC-remoderator-based trapping scheme more than doubles the trapping efficiency, contributing to a more than threefold increase in the positron accumulation rate compared with the original configuration.

item.title: A muonium laser ionization system for muon acceleration studies at J-PARC
item.description: arXiv:2611.30375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper reports the development and commissioning of a muonium ionization laser system installed in the H2 area of the J-PARC Materials and Life Science Experimental Facility for muon accelerator studies. In this accelerator scheme, ultraslow muons generated by laser ionization of thermal muonium atoms serve as the particle source for subsequent radio-frequency acceleration. The laser system generates coherent 122-nm pulses for muonium excitation and 355-nm pulses for photoionization of the excited muonium. A vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) pulse transport system and VUV pulse diagnostics were also developed. Muonium ionization was confirmed using a 5.7~keV muon transport line, and a muon rate of approximately 6~s$^{-1}$ was observed. These results establish operation of the ionization system and provide a platform for subsequent muon accelerator studies.
item.dc:creator: Shusei Kamioka, Meng Lyu, Katsuyoshi Homma, Tsutomu Mibe, Shinki Nakamura, Yu Oishi, Koichiro Shimomura, Tatsuya Shinozaki, Hikaru Sunagawa, Satoshi Wada, Takumi Yamada, Takayuki Yamazaki

item.title: FGPA-based advanced muon trigger algorithms for long-lived particle detection at the High-Luminosity LHC
item.description: arXiv:2611.30394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The CMS Level-1 trigger must reconstruct muons in real time under stringent latency and hardware resource constraints. Conventional algorithms lose efficiency for high-energy muons undergoing radiative energy losses and can be suboptimal for displaced trajectories, limiting sensitivity to exotic signatures such as long-lived particles (LLPs). The Phase-2 upgrade introduces advanced FPGAs that enable more sophisticated reconstruction algorithms. This work presents two complementary developments addressing these challenges. In the barrel region, a dedicated algorithm detects showers from Drift Tube hit patterns at the first processing stage. At the subsequent filtering stage, shower primitives are correlated with conventional trigger primitives, currently targeting radiatively showering high-momentum muons, with LLP signatures as a broader objective. Simulation studies yield approximately $80\%$ shower-classification accuracy and an estimated matching efficiency above $80\%$ for radiating muons. Firmware prototypes demonstrate a shower-detection latency of approximately $20\,\mathrm{ns}$ and sub-bunch-crossing latency for preliminary matching logic. In parallel, a hardware-oriented optimization methodology is investigated for future graph neural network based displaced-muon reconstruction in the barrel--endcap overlap region. Using a GraphSAGE proxy on a benchmark dataset, a workflow combining integer quantization, power-of-two scaling, and data-driven bit-width optimization achieves $(75.0 \pm 1.1)\%$ accuracy and a deterministic latency of $19$ cycles ($52.8\,\mathrm{ns}$ at $360\,\mathrm{MHz}$), with only $20\%$ digital signal processor utilization. These results establish a basis for implementation studies using CMS muon data.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Estrada (for the CMS Collaboration), Javier Prado (for the CMS Collaboration), Pelayo Leguina (for the CMS Collaboration), Andrea Cardini (for the CMS Collaboration), Elena Aller (for the CMS Collaboration), Santiago Folgueras (for the CMS Collaboration)

item.title: Efficient phase-only wavefront shaping at 250 kHz for multimode fiber endomicroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.29015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wavefront shaping through multimode fibers (MMFs) enables diffraction-limited fluorescence imaging with hair-thin probes, at a speed and light budget bounded by the wavefront modulator. Existing modulators provide at most two of three key characteristics: high refresh rate, (high) modal dimensionality, and light efficiency. Here, we demonstrate wavefront control through an MMF using a tailored phase-only microelectromechanical modulator that combines all three, with 8,192 elements arranged in a 32 x 256 array, 7-bit phase control, and a 250 kHz full-frame refresh rate. Direct on-axis phase modulation delivers 70+/-5% of the incident light into the modulated field and eliminates both off-axis encoding optical losses and hologram computation. The generated foci at the distal end of the fiber remain isotropic with high fidelity. We use singular-value decomposition analysis of the measured transmission to identify the effective degrees of freedom of our system. By scanning the focus at multiple depths, we demonstrate volumetric fluorescence imaging. These results open a new operating regime for adaptive in vivo multimode-fiber endoscopy.
item.dc:creator: Pau Riera Rodr\'iguez, Antonio M. Caravaca-Aguirre, Omer Tzang, Alexander Payne, Stephen Hamann, Rafael Piestun

item.title: Ultrabroadband, high-sensitivity time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy enabled by a Yb-based laser system
item.description: arXiv:2611.29295v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ultrafast optical fields have introduced numerous novel light-induced states in quantum materials. Identifying these states and elucidating their formation mechanisms require comprehensive, quantitative access to nonequilibrium electrodynamics across relevant energy scales. Here, we develop a Yb-laser-based time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy (TRTS) platform combining multi-pass-cell pulse compression, spintronic terahertz generation, and air-biased coherent detection. A single time-domain waveform scan provides continuous phase-resolved spectral coverage to 25 THz ($\sim$100 meV) with a Fourier resolution of 0.1 THz ($\sim$0.4 meV). This capability enables the characterization of both low-frequency charge dynamics and higher-energy resonant excitations in quantum materials under a common temporal reference. The system achieves a single-scan time-domain signal-to-noise ratio of 72 dB with long-term waveform stability, while preserving most of the laser pulse energy for tunable excitation. Measurements on intrinsic GaAs resolve extremely weak phonon features above 23 THz and demonstrate quantitative retrieval of equilibrium and transient complex optical properties. The resulting platform can provide a more complete microscopic picture of light-induced states in quantum materials.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Yuan Wu, Si-Jia Li, Jing-Long Ma, Guo-Qian Liao, Alexander Holm Ohrt, Long Cheng, Peter Uhd Jepsen, Bin-Bin Zhou, Si-Jie Zhang, Yu-Tong Li

item.title: Ballistic propagation-mediated super-resolution light-element imaging: in-situ tracking dynamic hydrogen migration
item.description: arXiv:2611.29563v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transmission electrons - with few-picometer wavelengths - can theoretically resolve all atoms in solids. However, constrained by factors such as lens aberrations, Z-contrast dependence and poor temporal resolution, the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) fails to tackle the long-standing challenge of hydrogen dynamics on atomic scale. Here, our experiment-guided simulations reveal that unlike heavy-atom imaging - governed by wave-based imaging process - ballistic propagation of particle-like electrons in Cs-corrected TEM enables super-resolution imaging (SRI) of light atoms, achieving a resolution down to 14 pm and a robust hydrogen contrast of ~24%. Our in-situ SRI study not only uncovers polymetric hydrogen aggregation in TiHx and H-LaAlO3, but also inter-site migration, rotational displacement of hydrogen species and collective hydrogen tunneling-induced polarization surge in the oxide. By exploiting the novel electron-matter interactions, our findings offer an unparalleled approach to probe hydrogen dynamics and establish accurate structure-property relationships in diverse functional materials.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyao Liang, Feng Liu, Linyuan Chen, Zhiwei Lv, Shiya Chen, Xinyu Liao, Yuzhou He, Yi Wang, Pengpeng Liu, Hua Bing Tao, Nianpeng Lu, Changlin Zheng, Yang Sun, Qinghua Zhang, Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski, Xian-Kui Wei

item.title: Toward Neutrino and Dark Matter Detection with Ancient Minerals: TEM Study of Heavy-Ion Tracks in Olivine
item.description: arXiv:2604.09732v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Solar, supernova, and atmospheric neutrinos, and possibly weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter, have been interacting in the Earth beneath our feet for billions of years. The ''paleo-detector'' technique seeks to detect and characterize the induced crystalline defects from these events, in particular from energetic nuclear recoils, which in some minerals can be preserved on these timescales. Such defects can manifest as nuclear recoil tracks, on the order of a few nanometers wide and extending up to hundreds of microns in length, which can be detected with nanoscale-resolution microscopy. In order to test the feasibility of the paleo-detector technique and to study the formation and morphology of track defects in promising mineral candidates like olivine, we use ion irradiation to artificially implant tracks to effectively mimic astrophysical particle interactions. We present a study of heavy-ion track width as a function of depth, which we relate to ion energy, in an olivine crystal irradiated with 15 MeV Au$^{+5}$ using scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Unlike previous studies, which measure tracks at the surface of the irradiated sample, we instead take measurements at various target depths via focused ion-beam sectioning of the irradiated sample. No etching techniques are used to enhance the tracks. In addition, we provide a comparison to predictions from simulations using SRIM software and previous results with a variety of ion species and energies. Notably, we find that a significant change in track continuity across the energy range studied (0.4-12.9 MeV) is indicative of the transition between electronic and nuclear stopping power dominance, consistent with the simulations' predictions. Overall, the tracks produced in olivine indicate that this mineral is an attractive candidate for paleo-detection, with robust track creation at the MeV scale.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Calabrese-Day, Emilie LaVoie-Ingram, Kathryn Ream, Hannah Ross, Joshua Spitz, Patrick Stengel, Kai Sun, Alexander Takla

item.title: Proposing, never assigning: fair allocation of shifts in experimental particle physics collaborations from ranked wishes under institutional quotas
item.description: arXiv:2609.19658v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Experimental particle physics collaborations staff the operation of their detectors with shifts, taken in the control room or remotely by members drawn from dozens of institutions. The established practice for filling them is a credit system with self sign-up: institutions owe a quota of credit, and people take the seats they want when booking opens. This paper describes a method in which seats are instead allocated from ranked wishes under institutional quotas, the result is issued as offers that each person accepts or declines, and an independent checker recomputes every rule before anything is published: the platform proposes, never assigns, and proves that it kept the rules. The credit and quota model is inherited from current practice. Around that core the paper adds a quota rule that keeps indivisible blocks fair to institutions whose share of a period is smaller than one block, and four rules that make fairness visible beyond the count: shares of owl, weekend and holiday blocks, seats shown in the laboratory's clock and the institution's own, reachable pools for institutions that cannot travel, and booking order by balance. On a synthetic collaboration of 48 institutions and 256 eligible members, the method allocates 70 to 72 of 72 seats per period in two rounds, with a mean rank satisfaction of 84 to 95% and no rule broken; after a year of running every institution of four members or more is within 13% of its cumulative share, and the smallest institutions, which one block overshoots by arithmetic, are brought within the same range by pooling in pairs. The method is stated completely enough to be reimplemented; a reference implementation exists and is available to collaborations under license. It applies as it stands to any scientific collaboration that staffs a facility in blocks of shifts under institutional quotas.
item.dc:creator: Kamal Benslama

item.title: Leveraging Industrial Foundation Models at the Edge of Particle Physics Detectors via Distillation Learning and Hardware Co-design
item.description: arXiv:2609.23385v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Data acquisition (DAQ) systems at future particle physics experiments stand to benefit from the extremes of AI/ML development: large-scale foundation models can enhance the performance of feature extraction algorithms, and small-scale on-detector deployments can enable real-time intelligent data handling. This work provides the first tokenizer fine-tuning of an industrial foundation model for particle physics DAQ. Starting from the backbone of Google Research's TimesFM (Time Series Foundation Model), we address real-time regression tasks for drift chamber trackers and dual-readout calorimeters by jointly training the pretrained tokenizer and a newly initialized residual adapter, then fitting task-specific linear heads while keeping the transformer backbone frozen. Furthermore, the resulting TimesFM teachers can be distilled into students and co-designed with FPGA implementation to support real-time operation at future colliders. The distilled and compressed models achieve competitive performance, while distillation reduces reliance on labeled training data. Further, the pipeline of distillation and model compression from TimesFM is generic and can be easily adapted to a variety of 1D waveform tasks across domains.
item.dc:creator: Gia Ancone, Qibin Liu, Liangyu Wu, Julia Gonski

item.title: Impact of Gain Layer Doping Concentration on the Performance of 4H-SiC LGADs
item.description: arXiv:2610.00824v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gain layer doping concentration determines the electric field profile in a low gain avalanche detector (LGAD) and is therefore the primary design parameter. This work reports its influence on the charge collection and timing behavior of 4H-SiC LGADs. Two mesa-isolated devices with cold He ion implanted termination differ only in gain layer doping, $4\times10^{17}$~$cm^{-3}$ and $5\times10^{17}$~$cm^{-3}$, and are characterized together with a PIN diode from the same wafer using the ultraviolet transient current technique (UV-TCT). The 25\% doping difference produces a gain difference of about two orders of magnitude at the same applied bias, representing a gain range of 3.7 to 216. Under UV-TCT excitation, the higher-doped device exhibits time-resolution minima within a gain range of about 20--80 across the investigated laser intensities, consistent with the transition from electronic-noise-dominated jitter to multiplication shot noise. The non-monotonic timing response is also observed under a $^{90}Sr$ beta source with a Si LGAD reference: the higher-doped device reaches 51.7 ps at 280 V and then degrades, while the lower-doped device requires more than 450 V. This measured gain window provides an experimental reference for further optimization of the gain-layer design.
item.dc:creator: Tao Yang, Ben J. Sekely, Yashas Satapathy, Abraham Tishelman-Charny, Greg Allion, Gil Atar, Philip Barletta, Gabriele Giacomini, Carl Haber, Steve Holland, John F. Muth, Spyridon Pavlidis, Chengxi Yang, Haichen Wang, Stefania Stucci

item.title: Rotating Capacitive System for Measurement of a Third Order Gravity Gradient Based on a Single-Axis Mechanical Oscillator. Part I, Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.22162v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is a feasibility study on a single-axis mechanical oscillator, mounted on a miniature circular rotating platform, that is proposed to be used for measuring a quantity proportional to the second vertical derivative of gravitational acceleration projected onto the oscillator's sensitivity axis. The latter is aligned with the axis of rotation. Part I establishes theoretical feasibility only. Design constraints, quantitative sensitivity, error budgets, and mobile platform performance will be addressed in Part II.
item.dc:creator: Alexey V. Veryaskin, Khyl J. McMahon, Howard C. Golden

item.title: Wavelet-domain flow-matching posterior estimation for LISA signals with data gaps
item.description: arXiv:2512.18290v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) data stream will contain scheduled and unscheduled gaps, which break the stationarity of the instrumental noise and invalidate the standard frequency-domain likelihood. Amortized simulation-based inference (SBI) avoids explicit likelihood evaluations, but its application to months-long observations requires compressing high-dimensional, gapped time series while preserving information about source parameters. We develop an end-to-end amortized posterior estimation pipeline: the gapped data are mapped to noise-scaled Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) wavelet coefficients and summarized by a convolutional-Transformer network, trained jointly with a flow-matching (FM) posterior estimator, with optional importance-sampling correction. For a LISA-like signal observed for 3 months, the amortized FM posteriors are well calibrated on simulated observations whose waveforms and gaps were not seen in training. The FM posteriors agree closely with the benchmark, the posteriors from parallel-tempered Markov chain Monte Carlo (PTMCMC), although they exhibit moderately greater dispersion. Importance sampling efficiently reweights the FM posterior, achieving close agreement with the benchmark at modest additional cost.
item.dc:creator: Ruiting Mao, Jeong Eun Lee, Matthew C. Edwards

item.title: Neural Field Thermal Tomography: A Differentiable Physics Framework for Non-Destructive Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2603.11045v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Inverse problems for stiff parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs), such as the inverse heat conduction problem (IHCP), are severely ill-posed: the forward map rapidly damps high-frequency interior structure before it reaches the boundary. Soft-constrained physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), which embed the PDE as a residual penalty, decouple the diffusivity from the surface data in their standard two-network inverse formulation, and the evaluated variants fit boundary measurements while leaving the interior field essentially untouched. We propose Neural Field Thermal Tomography (NeFTY), a hard-constrained neural field framework for label-free three-dimensional inverse heat conduction. NeFTY represents the unknown diffusivity as a continuous coordinate-based neural network, and at every optimization step passes the candidate field through a differentiable implicit-Euler heat solver with harmonic-mean interface flux, so that the simulated temperature satisfies the discretized heat equation up to the solver tolerance. Adjoint gradients propagate the surface reconstruction error back to the network weights at solver-level memory cost, making test-time inversion tractable on a single GPU. Across synthetic 3D benchmarks, NeFTY outperforms soft-constrained PINN variants, a voxel-grid baseline, and classical L-BFGS voxel inversion through the same solver on label-free volumetric recovery, and it transfers to real thermography data, surpassing classical signal-processing baselines in both defect segmentation and depth estimation. Additional details at https://cab-lab-princeton.github.io/nefty/
item.dc:creator: Tao Zhong, Yixun Hu, Dongzhe Zheng, Aditya Sood, Christine Allen-Blanchette

item.title: Complete virtual unwrapping and reading of a rolled Herculaneum papyrus
item.description: arXiv:2606.29085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The carbonized papyrus scrolls from Herculaneum preserve the only large-scale library to survive from classical antiquity. Many scrolls have remained unread because physical unrolling risks irreversible damage. Non-invasive imaging offers a route to their texts, yet previous work on sealed Herculaneum scrolls has recovered only localized readings. Here, by combining high-resolution X-ray computed microtomography ($\mu$CT) data acquired on the BM18 beamline at the ESRF with machine-learning-assisted virtual unwrapping, we study three still-closed scrolls. For PHerc. 1667, a remnant of earlier attempts at physical unrolling, we achieve the complete unwrapping and reading of the preserved writing surface, making it the first Herculaneum papyrus read completely by virtual unwrapping. The text was transcribed and cross-verified by nine papyrologists. In PHerc. Paris. 4, the source of the Vesuvius Challenge 2023 Grand Prize text, the high-resolution scan makes ink directly visible in the tomographic volume, allowing 3D ink segmentation and comparison of recovered text with visible deposits. In PHerc. 139, we recover title and author-attribution evidence identifying the scroll as Philodemus, On Gods, Book 8. These results establish a basis for the ongoing, systematic recovery and scholarly study of texts preserved within the still-closed Herculaneum library.

item.title: Nanohertz Loss in a Pendulum for Macroscopic Entanglement under Structural Damping
item.description: arXiv:2608.02462v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Pendulums are attractive for macroscopic quantum control because gravitational dissipation dilution lowers the modal loss, while the $1/f$ force noise of structural damping allows nearly lossless trapping to suppress the noise at an upshifted resonance. The same $1/f$ spectrum, however, produces a low-frequency tail that penalizes entanglement. To overcome this penalty, we realize a 7-mg pendulum suspended by a stepped fused-silica fiber. Ring-down measurements give an energy-decay rate $\Gamma/2\pi=361(39)$ nHz at the bare resonance $\omega_0/2\pi=2.63$ Hz. The reduction in $\omega_0\Gamma$ relative to the previous uniform suspension more than offsets the penalty. Although both suspensions support entanglement in the error-free model, only the stepped one allows robust verification in the multimode model with experimental uncertainties.
item.dc:creator: Azusa Sawada, Hina Nakano, Kanta Watanabe, Gaku Ohashi, Shota Okumura, Nobuyuki Matsumoto

item.title: Analysis of CONUS+ run 2: Detector performance, background model and CE$\nu$NS measurement
item.description:
arXiv:2610.37345v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$
u$NS) provides a uniquely sensitive probe of neutrino properties, but its detection requires pushing energy thresholds to the sub-keV scale while controlling backgrounds. The CONUS+ experiment, located at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, reported the first observation of CE$
u$NS using reactor antineutrinos in 2025. Following a detector upgrade that replaced three of the original 1 kg high-purity germanium detectors with larger 2.42 kg diodes, this paper presents the analysis of the CONUS+ run 2 dataset, including the detector characterization, the background model, the signal prediction and expected sensitivity, and the extraction of the CE$
u$NS signal. The new detectors reach a background level per unit mass reduced by approximately a factor of two relative to the original detectors, while reaching energy thresholds between 140 and 170 eV$_{ee}$. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on and 86 kg$\cdot$days reactor-off, a blind likelihood analysis fitting directly the number of signal counts yields $N_s = 1565 \pm 155$ CE$
u$NS events and a relative precision of 9.9\%. The result is in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events, with $N_s/N_{\mathrm{SM}} = 0.92 \pm 0.14$.

item.title: momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
item.description: arXiv:2611.25888v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $\Delta t$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.
